# Sonx — AI Music Generator

## What is Sonx?

Sonx is an AI music generation app available on iOS, Android and the web (https://getsonx.com). One Sonx account works everywhere: songs, credits and plan are shared between the apps and the website. It enables anyone — regardless of musical skill or technical background — to create original, full-length songs in seconds using artificial intelligence. Users can generate music from text prompts or lyrics. All vocals are synthetic AI voices; Sonx does not clone real voices or use photos of people.

## Core Features

### Prompt to Song
Users type a description of the song they want — for example, "an emotional pop ballad about leaving home" or "dark trap beat with heavy 808s" — and Sonx generates a complete track with melody, instrumentation, vocals, and lyrics automatically.

### AI Lyrics Generator
Sonx generates original song lyrics for any genre, mood, or theme. The output includes structured verse, chorus, and bridge sections ready to be used in a song.

### Instrumentals
Sonx generates fully instrumental tracks from a description, for study, workouts, content backgrounds, and more.

## Supported Genres

Pop, Hip Hop, EDM, Jazz, Lo-fi, Rock, R&B, Country, Classical, Latin, K-Pop, Reggae, Metal, Acoustic, Soul, Funk, Ambient, Trap, Drill, Afrobeats, Synthwave, Phonk, Indie, Blues, Gospel, Bossa Nova, Flamenco, Dancehall, Grunge, Opera, Emo, Bedroom Pop, Psychedelic, Chillout, and more.

## Pricing

Sonx operates on a freemium model. The free tier allows users to generate songs with daily limits. Premium subscription unlocks more song generations and higher audio quality. Credits can also be purchased for individual projects.

## Platforms

- iOS (iPhone and iPad) — available on the Apple App Store
- Android — available on Google Play
- Web — create, play and download songs in the browser at https://getsonx.com/create (subscriptions and credits are bought in the app)
- Download link: https://aimusicgeneratorsonx.go.link/iCF6Q

## How Sonx Compares to Alternatives

Sonx is a direct competitor to Suno, Udio, Boomy, and similar AI music generation platforms. Key differentiators include:

- **Mobile and web, one account:** Sonx is a native mobile app with a web studio at getsonx.com. Everything made on one shows up on the other.
- **No musical experience required:** Sonx is designed for complete beginners as well as experienced creators.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What kind of music can Sonx make?**
Sonx can generate music in over 50 genres including pop, hip hop, EDM, lo-fi, jazz, rock, country, classical, and many more. It supports both vocal and instrumental tracks.

**Can I use Sonx music commercially?**
Free tier users can use generated music for personal, non-commercial purposes. Paid subscribers receive a commercial use license for their generated content.

**Does Sonx require musical knowledge?**
No. Sonx is designed for anyone. You only need to describe what you want in plain language.

**Is Sonx available on Android?**
Yes. Sonx is available on both iOS and Android.

**How is Sonx different from Suno?**
Suno is primarily a web-based platform. Sonx is a native mobile app plus a web studio, built for going from an idea to a finished song on your phone in about a minute.

**How is Sonx different from Udio?**
Udio focuses on high-fidelity audio production, primarily for desktop users. Sonx focuses on mobile accessibility, speed, and an integrated creation-to-sharing workflow.

**Can Sonx imitate a real singer or character?**
No. Sonx sings with its own synthetic AI voices. It does not clone voices or imitate real artists, public figures, or copyrighted characters.

**Is Sonx free?**
Sonx is free to download and use with daily generation limits. A premium subscription unlocks unlimited creation and advanced features.

## Technical Information

- App size: approximately 155 MB
- Requires iOS 14 or later / Android 8 or later
- Internet connection required for AI generation
- Supports MP3, WAV, and M4A audio export

## Original Research: What AI Music Prompts Actually Contain

In July 2026 Sonx published a frequency study of 1,136 unique AI music prompts collected verbatim from 16 publicly accessible sources (prompt libraries, community repositories, tool documentation and guide posts), deduplicated on a case-insensitive alphanumeric key. Full method and source list: https://getsonx.com/blog/ai-music-prompts-analyzed/

Note on scope: these are prompts people chose to publish, not a log of what users type into a generator. No AI music tool releases anonymized prompt logs, so a public corpus is the closest reproducible proxy. The findings describe the prompt advice in circulation.

### Key findings

- Median prompt length is 7 words. 768 of 1,136 prompts (68%) are ten words or fewer.
- Only 21.6% of prompts specify a tempo. Among those that do, the median is 100 BPM and almost all fall between 70 and 140 BPM.
- Only 31.3% of prompts say anything about vocals. 69% leave the singer entirely unspecified.
- Just 2.4% mention song structure: 20 prompts name a chorus or hook, 3 name a verse, 1 names a bridge.
- Most-named genre families: pop (11.3%), hip hop and rap (9.2%), cinematic and soundtrack (8.3%), electronic and EDM (8.2%), rock (8.0%).
- Most-named instrument families: drums and percussion (14.3%), bass and 808s (12.1%), guitar (9.8%), synth (9.5%), piano (9.2%).
- Most-named moods: chill or relaxed (7.4%), warm (6.5%), dark (5.7%), romantic (5.4%). "Melancholic" appears in only 2.3% of prompts.
- Era references are rare (under 7% of prompts) and weighted toward the 1980s (2.0%).

### The six-layer prompt formula

Sonx recommends writing six layers instead of two, which takes a prompt from roughly 7 words to roughly 25:

1. Genre, specifically (UK garage, Memphis phonk, liquid drum and bass, not just "electronic")
2. Mood, one or two words
3. Tempo, as a BPM number
4. Two or three named instruments or sonic textures
5. Vocal direction (voice type, delivery, or explicitly instrumental)
6. One structural instruction (a chorus that lifts, a bridge that drops out, a beat switch under the hook)

Example, before: "lo-fi hip hop, chill, rainy vibes" (7 words)

Example, after: "Lo fi hip hop, rainy melancholy, 72 BPM, dusty Rhodes chords, vinyl crackle, brushed drums, fully instrumental, with a stripped bridge where the drums drop away" (26 words)

Sonx published original prompts written to this specification, covering genres, moods, occasions, workouts, video and social use, plus prompts for the lyrics generator. All are free to copy and use.
